label: Zen Page Tint
Adaptive chrome color from the active page. Settings marked “restart” take effect after Zen is restarted; the rest apply instantly.
Appearance — applies live
Tint strength (0–100): page color laid as an overlay over your Zen theme. 100 = full page color, 0 = your untouched Zen theme/gradient.
Saturation (0–200): vibrancy of the tint. 0 = grayscale, 100 = the page's own, 200 = double.
Brightness (0–300): gain on the tint's lightness. 100 = as sampled, 200 = twice as light. Applied before the lightness clamps below.
Contrast (0–300): pushes the tint away from mid-grey. 100 = as sampled, 200 = double, 0 = flat grey.

Ambient spread (0–100): directional gradient strength. The chrome takes color from the matching side of the page instead of one flat average — left of the URL bar from the left of the page, top of the sidebar from the top. 0 = off (flat tint).
Minimum lightness (0–100): floor so near-black pages don't make the chrome muddy. 0 = no floor.
Maximum lightness (0–100): cap so blinding-white pages don't wash the chrome out. 100 = no cap.
Disable on these sites (comma-separated hosts; supports *.example.com). The chrome keeps your Zen theme on them.
Frame gap (px): non-compact mode only. Compact mode stays flush so edge-hover controls keep working.
Frame corner radius (px).
Color source — applies live
On YouTube, follow video colors while the player's Ambient mode is enabled. Excludes padding around the video; falls back to normal page sampling when Ambient mode is off.

Average pages as light rather than flat color (brighter, more saturated on mixed pages — a mostly-dark page with bright content stops reading as dark). The YouTube ambient source always uses this model.
Live mode — follow video / animated pages (restart)
Enable live mode (continuously follow video / animated content).
Always poll, not only while a video is playing (higher idle cost).
Color change rate (ms): how often the tint can change while polling. Used exactly as set. Keep it at or above the fade duration below, or fades get cut off before they finish.
Re-tint threshold (0–255): minimum per-channel color change needed to re-tint while polling.
Color fade duration (ms) applied to every tint change.
Always-on host allowlist (comma-separated) for canvas/WebGL players and cross-origin video embeds. Supports *.example.com.
Advanced (restart)
Debug logging to the Browser Console (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-J).
